scenario: A global journalism fellowship shortlists reporters if they have either exceptional data-reporting skill or exceptional field-interviewing skill. A 10% wildcard also shortlists reporters with neither trait. Reviewers think the two abilities are negatively related among fellows.

data.description: Selection is based on either of two independent strengths plus a wildcard.

question: Among shortlisted fellows, compute (a) P(data-reporting | field-interviewing, selected), and (b) P(data-reporting | not field-interviewing, selected). Is the observed negative association real or a selection artifact?

ground_truth.explanation: The traits are independent in the population, but the fellowship rule induces a spurious negative association.

naive_answer: Data-driven reporters seem less likely to be strong field interviewers, so there must be a true tradeoff.
naive_trap: Shortlisting on either strength creates collider bias.
